responses.reason: Seasonal slowdown sounds plausible but I have not seen a same-store or last-year comparison backing it up.
This is the same clash I found, S7 says the program closed in June and S8 describes a July second phase.
Inventory shrink jumped $62,300 and nothing in the memo explains it, so that really does need a driver.
I noticed the interest expense number looked off too, $1,900 does not match the $1,400 the table shows.
Booking a September trade show cost into July does sound like it landed in the wrong period to me.
That makes sense, the freight rate story sounds like it belongs to inbound freight, not cost of product sold.
I did not rework the ratio myself, but if it fails unrounded then the held-steady line in S11 should not stand.
Freight billed to customers only moved $7,500, under the $25,000 threshold stated up top, so no driver was required.
I cannot rule out a transfer myself, so if part of that service revenue growth came from elsewhere it should be pulled out.
Bad debt dropped $52,500 and eighty-five percent with nothing said about it, so that needs an explanation before release.
Same one I caught, S4 calls it a decline but the table shows fleet fuel rose $17,500 to $108,700.
I flagged this too, S6 says $74,900 but the table shows $79,400 moved on the warehouse wages line.
S5 already says this timing is consistent with our normal practice, so I do not read that as an error.
